title: 312 Shows in a Year to $775.6 Million
description:
Ed Sheeran's Divide Tour made 775.6 million dollars, the highest-grossing tour ever at its end in 2019.

Sources:
- Pollstar: Ed Sheeran Concludes 'Divide' Tour, Sets All-Time Touring Record At $775.6M: https://news.pollstar.com/2019/08/27/ed-sheeran-concludes-divide-tour-sets-all-time-touring-record-at-775-6m/
- Express & Star: Ed Sheeran set for Wolverhampton Civic gigs: https://www.expressandstar.com/entertainment/music/2012/01/16/ed-sheeran-set-for-wolverhampton-civic-gigs/
- Wikipedia: Ed Sheeran: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ed_Sheeran
- Wikipedia: ÷ Tour: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%B7_Tour

From the cited pages: Sheeran moved to London in 2008 and began playing in small venues; he said "I played 312 shows in 2009," sometimes to no one, or five people, often to more; the Divide Tour ended on August 26, 2019 with 775.6 million dollars on 8.9 million tickets at 255 performances over two and a half years, per Pollstar; the previous record was U2's 360 Tour at 735.3 million dollars. Other outlets report slightly different totals (Billboard: 776.4 million). Not financial advice.

first_comment: Would you play a show for five people to chase a record? 👇

scenes.narration: Ed Sheeran once played a show for five people. So how did his tour make 775.6 million dollars, a record back then?
He played 312 shows in one year.
He plays guitar in tiny rooms, night after night.
Then his Divide Tour sells 8.9 million tickets.
That beats U2's old record of 735.3 million dollars.
